Title: AI Engineer
Location: San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León, Mexico
Description: Johnson Controls International (JCI) is seeking an AI Engineer to join our innovative and impact-driven Data Science and Analytics team. This role is ideal for an engineer who combines solid software, data, and ML engineering skills with hands-on Generative AI experience—and a data scientist's curiosity for how models behave. You build the pipelines, tooling, and applications that turn AI and LLM models into dependable production software. As an AI Engineer, you will independently own the end-to-end delivery of defined AI projects—from data pipeline through deployed application. You will make sound technical decisions within your scope, partner directly with cross-functional stakeholders, and guide junior engineers on specific problems as you deliver measurable business value. How You Will Do It Generative AI Systems & Applications Develop and deploy Generative AI systems and LLM-powered applications (e.g., GPT, Claude, LLaMA) for use cases such as enterprise search, document summarization, and conversational AI. Apply prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and orchestration techniques to adapt foundation models for domain-specific applications. Build agentic workflows and task-specific AI agents—using Palantir AIP or the Microsoft Agent Framework—that orchestrate tools, retrieval, and reasoning. Evaluate and improve model outputs for accuracy, relevance, latency, and cost, applying data science techniques to measure and validate performance. Data, ML & Software Engineering Build and maintain the data pipelines that feed AI systems—ingestion, transformation, and ETL across structured and unstructured sources (e.g., Snowflake, Azure). Develop and operate ML pipelines and MLOps workflows—training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring—using CI/CD, containerization (Docker), and model serving. Build reusable components, services, and APIs around AI models that help the team ship features faster. Implement retrieval and embedding workflows (RAG, vector databases) for scalable, accurate knowledge retrieval. Apply software engineering best practices—testing, version control, and code review—across your projects. Business Impact & Stakeholder Communication Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to translate business challenges into AI solutions. Support workshops and proofs-of-concept that demonstrate the value of LLM and agent use cases across business units. Translate model outputs, data findings, and technical tradeoffs into clear insights for non-technical audiences. Mentorship & Collaboration Guide junior engineers on specific technical problems and code quality. Contribute to design discussions and technical decisions within the team. Share knowledge and help raise the bar on engineering and data science practices. Qualifications & Experience Education in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical or quantitative discipline. 2–5 years of experience in software, data, ML engineering, or data science, including hands-on work with LLMs or generative AI. Demonstrated success delivering data or ML pipelines and AI/ML solutions to production. Experience with data science fundamentals—exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, or classic ML (classification, regression, forecasting). Experience with cloud AI platforms such as Azure OpenAI/Azure ML, AWS SageMaker/Bedrock, or Google Cloud Vertex AI. Technical Expertise Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with good software engineering habits—testing, version control, and clean code. Hands-on experience with the Generative AI stack: prompt engineering, fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), LLM orchestration, and agent frameworks (LangChain, Semantic Kernel, Microsoft Agent Framework). Experience building ETL and ML pipelines and applying MLOps practices (CI/CD, Docker, model serving). Familiarity with data science libraries and workflows—pandas, scikit-learn, and model evaluation and experimentation. Experience with JCI's stack—or comparable platforms—including Palantir AIP, Azure ML, Microsoft Agent Framework, Power Automate, and Snowflake. Working knowledge of embeddings, vector databases, and retrieval systems. Soft Skills Ability to own projects and communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs clearly. Strong collaboration skills across product, engineering, and business teams. Comfortable presenting technical and analytical work to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Self-directed problem solver who manages priorities independently. Preferred Qualifications Experience with IoT, edge analytics, or smart building systems. Familiarity with LLMOps, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, or similar orchestration frameworks. Data science depth—statistical modeling, experimentation, or deep learning (forecasting, computer vision, or NLP). Experience with the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365 Copilot, SharePoint, Power Platform, Snowflake). Knowledge of data privacy and governance considerations for enterprise LLM usage. Title: (CEN) SR PROCESS SPECIALIST
Location: Villa de García, Nuevo León, Mexico
Description: Job Description Make SmartOps optimization and anomaly detection models work in CEMEX cement plants, and keep them working. As the production and quality expert of the SmartOps program, specify and validate models with data scientists, confirm plant readiness, commission solutions on site, and coach plant teams until gains in yield, heat and power consumption, quality stability, and safety are verified against baseline. Build the repeatable method that lets each new plant start from what worked at the last one. Main Responsibilities CEMEX Values & Leadership: Work following the Mission, Vision, and Values of CEMEX, leading by example across all corporate and plant-level interactions. Process models Model specification: Work with data scientists and control specialists to define each model's variables, time delays, constraints, and valid operating ranges for raw mix, grinding, kiln, and cement quality. Set quality targets from LSF, moduli, free lime, fineness, and strength, and ground the logic in process chemistry and heat and mass balances. Anomaly detection: Design detection rules and models for abnormal process behavior, false air, refractory condition, and quality drift. Validate them against real events, measure false alerts, missed events, and warning time, and assign a response owner to each alert. Work with maintenance and reliability specialists where process and equipment anomalies overlap, such as mill overload. Validation and lifecycle: Test models on historical data and plant trials against agreed acceptance criteria before release. Afterward, track performance, use root cause analysis (RCA) on gaps and operator overrides, and update logic when raw materials, fuels, products, or equipment change. Keep approved versions on record, with agreed fallback and retuning rules. Remote monitoring and advisory: When not on site, review model alerts, autopilot utilization, and operator overrides across plants from Monterrey. Send recommendations to plant teams and escalate when they are not acted on. Plant readiness Minimum requirements and audits: Define the minimum instrumentation, automation, and data each SmartOps use case needs, from sensor accuracy and calibration to historian sampling and lab data. Before commissioning, audit the plant with site instrumentation and automation teams, check signals, tag mapping, and data availability, and support PID loop tuning and alarm optimization. Send validated changes to the owner of the CEMEX instrumentation catalog. Gap analysis and business cases: Rank gaps in sensors, actuators, analyzers, and data quality against SmartOps requirements. Build CAPEX or OPEX business cases with site teams and follow execution through field verification and acceptance. Deployment and adoption Hands-on implementation: Work beside operators, engineers, and maintenance teams on walkdowns, measurements, commissioning, tuning, and troubleshooting. Use mass and heat balances, fan and duct assessments, and false air audits to separate process, control, instrumentation, and model limits. Stay through stabilization, verify results in the field, and close corrective actions after handover. Plant leadership: Lead and coach Production, Quality, and Plant Managers through agreed deployment plans. Secure owners, resources, and deadlines, resolve competing priorities, and escalate unresolved commitments to the SmartOps program lead. Plant management keeps daily operating and line management accountability. Governance and benefits: Run daily follow-up during commissioning and regular reviews after handover. Track adoption, closed-loop (autopilot) utilization, overrides, and production and quality stability. With plant teams and Finance, verify gains in specific heat and power, alternative fuel substitution, reagent use, and grinding media and refractory life, within emissions limits. Capability building: Train users from Plant Managers to control room operators, at the equipment and in the control room, and check that they can apply what they learned. Leave local owners, operating guidance, and support routines in place. As a PI and Seeq power user, build use cases and baselines that plant engineers can reuse. Deployment template: Package each deployment for the next plant (model specification, readiness checklist, acceptance criteria, training material) and turn recurring diagnostics into online tools. Safety Safety outcomes: With Production, Quality, and Health and Safety teams, implement changes that reduce hazardous manual work and exposure to hot material, dust, and moving equipment, such as remote inspection, automated sampling, and steadier operation that cuts blockages and hot meal handling. Agree safety objectives before each trial and verify results with site Health and Safety, such as interventions avoided and exposure time reduced. Operating envelope: Define and validate operating constraints, equipment protection limits, and environmental boundaries for every model and control. Keep required interlocks and independent protections, set up operator override and safe fallback, and apply Management of Change (MoC) with site approval before release. Field safety: Follow local safety rules, CEMEX standards, and site procedures. Complete required training, wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and confirm risk assessments, permits, energy isolation, and competence before field tasks. Take part in safety committees and in near-miss and incident investigations linked to SmartOps work. New technology pilots Technology pilots: When assigned, evaluate sensing, machine vision, robotics, or process technologies. Run plant trials against an agreed baseline, test vendor claims under operating conditions, and recommend scale-up or discontinuation from the measured results. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemical, Process, Mechanical, Industrial, or Control and Automation Engineering, or in Chemistry. An advanced degree is a plus. Experience: 8+ years in cement plant operations with hands-on work in both production and quality, including 3+ years accountable for kiln, raw mill, or cement mill production or quality results as Superintendent, Quality Manager, Process Manager, or above. Plant Production Manager experience is strongly preferred. Languages and travel: Fluent English and Spanish, spoken and written. Valid passport and US business visa, or able to obtain them before start. Knowledge Skills And Abilities Production and quality credibility: Cement manufacturing experience across quality, operations, and maintenance, with the credibility to coach and challenge Production, Quality, and Plant Managers without line authority. Process diagnostics: Field process measurement, mass and heat balances, fan and false air assessments, and raw mix and clinker chemistry (LSF, moduli, clinker mineralogy, free lime). Able to lead RCA and turn findings into corrective actions. Models and APC: Plant-side owner of at least one Advanced Process Control (APC) or AI optimizer deployment on a kiln, mill, or raw mix: set its constraints, ran acceptance trials, and tracked utilization. Daily user of a process historian (PI System preferred) and DCS. Seeq and Python are a plus. Instrumentation and control: Practical experience with cement plant instrumentation (gas analyzers, kiln pyrometers, weigh feeders, cross-belt analyzers, and pressure, flow, and temperature transmitters), PID loop tuning, and minimum automation standards. Working conditions and physical requirements Working conditions Approximately 50% travel, mainly to US cement plants, for implementation, audits, trials, and follow-up. Assignments include sustained periods on site during commissioning and stabilization, with scheduled startup or shift support when required. When not traveling, works from the Monterrey offices supporting plants remotely. Exposure to heat, cold, noise, dust, and outdoor conditions during field work, with site controls and required PPE. Tobacco-free environment. Physical requirements Walks plant areas and climbs stairs across multi-story structures, such as preheater towers, while carrying portable instruments; also sits for office and remote work. Medium work, as defined in the ADA worksheet below. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear in order to communicate with employees/visitors as well as function safely around heavy rolling equipment. Must be capable of working at heights and in confined spaces. Must pass physical screening, hearing test, and drug/alcohol screen. Title: Private Capital Data Operations & AI Innovation Analyst
Description: Your Team Responsibilities Make an Impact at the Intersection of Financial Data, Technology & InnovationAbout the Team & Opportunity Are you passionate about financial data, energized by solving complex challenges, and excited about how AI is transforming the way we work? Join MSCI's Private Capital Solutions (PCS) team, where you'll play a key role in delivering the high-quality financial data that powers critical investment decisions for clients across the private capital industry. Our team sits at the intersection of financial expertise, cutting-edge technology, and client experience . We transform complex financial information into accurate, reliable, and actionable data, leveraging advanced technology, AI-powered tools, and strong analytical expertise to deliver exceptional results. In this role, you'll do more than oversee operations. You'll have the opportunity to lead improvements, influence how we work, solve meaningful client challenges, and help shape the future of AI-enabled financial data operations at MSCI. You'll collaborate with talented professionals across Data Operations, Product, Engineering, and Client Service, bringing together different perspectives to continuously improve our processes, strengthen data quality, and deliver an outstanding client experience. If you enjoy combining analytical thinking, technology, leadership, and continuous improvement, this is an opportunity to make a real impact. https://careers.msci.com/life-at-msci Your Key Responsibilities What You'll Do Drive Operational Excellence & Client Impact Take ownership of critical financial data operations, ensuring our Private Capital Solutions clients receive accurate, timely, and high-quality data. Be the go-to expert for complex client data challenges, using your analytical skills and problem-solving mindset to deliver effective solutions. Monitor operational performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and help the team consistently exceed quality and service expectations. Shape the Future of AI-Powered Data Operations Work hands-on with AI-enabled financial data extraction and validation tools, combining technology with human expertise to deliver reliable results. Help define what great data quality looks like by establishing quality benchmarks, strengthening validation frameworks, and ensuring transparency and auditability. Investigate complex data exceptions, uncover root causes, and develop sustainable solutions that improve accuracy and reduce recurring issues. Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, streamline workflows, and unlock new efficiencies through technology and innovation. Collaborate, Influence & Innovate Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Operations, and Client Service teams to solve challenges and improve the end-to-end client data experience. Turn operational insights and client feedback into meaningful recommendations that influence technology enhancements, workflows, and service improvements. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen data quality, operational controls, scalability, and overall team performance. Play an active role in evolving our financial data processes as new technologies and business needs emerge. Lead, Develop & Inspire Others Act as a trusted subject matter expert in private capital financial data, operational workflows, and AI-assisted data validation. Mentor and support Analysts and Associates, sharing your expertise, strengthening technical capabilities, and helping others grow. Promote a culture of ownership, collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning. Use performance insights, KPIs, and operational analytics to identify trends, communicate results, and help drive informed decisions. Why This Role Matters Financial data is at the heart of the decisions our clients make every day. Your work will directly contribute to the accuracy, reliability, and scalability of the data services they depend on. This is an opportunity to combine your financial and analytical expertise with emerging AI technologies, collaborate with teams across MSCI, and help build smarter, more efficient ways of working. If you're someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving challenging problems, developing others, and turning ideas into meaningful improvements, we'd love to hear from you. Your Skills And Experience That Will Help You Excel What You'll Bring to the Team We're looking for a curious, analytical, and solutions-oriented professional who thrives on solving complex challenges, embraces new technologies, and is passionate about making financial data smarter, more accurate, and more impactful. You'll be successful in this role if you bring a combination of financial expertise, technological curiosity, strong problem solving skills and a collaborative mindset. A strong foundation in finance and data: A bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Data Science, or a related field. At least 3-5 years of relevant experience in financial data operations, data management, client data services, or a similar financial services environment. A passion for AI and emerging technologies: Hands-on experience using AI-powered data extraction and validation tools, with the analytical judgment to challenge outputs, identify inconsistencies, and ensure data accuracy and reliability. A natural problem-solving mindset: You enjoy getting to the root of complex issues, navigating ambiguity, and turning operational challenges into opportunities for smarter, more efficient ways of working. The ability to connect people, processes, and technology: Experience driving cross-functional initiatives and building strong relationships with Technology, Product, Operations, and client-facing teams to deliver meaningful improvements. The confidence to communicate and influence: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex financial data concepts, share insights, and engage stakeholders across different levels and functions. An uncompromising commitment to quality: A sharp eye for detail and a disciplined approach to data integrity, quality assurance, operational controls, and auditability, including within AI-assisted workflows. An understanding of private markets: Knowledge of private capital data, fund administration, investment operations, or related financial datasets, and an interest in how high-quality data supports investment decisions. A technology-driven approach to efficiency: Experience working with financial data pipelines, workflow automation or orchestration tools, and cloud-based data environments, with an eagerness to explore better ways of working. A collaborative leadership style: Experience mentoring or guiding junior colleagues, sharing knowledge, encouraging continuous learning, and helping build a high-performing team. What Will Make You Stand Out Beyond your technical experience, we value individuals who bring curiosity, initiative, adaptability, and a continuous improvement mindset . You're someone who doesn't just identify problems, you take ownership of solving them. You're excited about the potential of AI, comfortable challenging existing processes, and motivated by opportunities to make a tangible impact. If you're ready to combine your financial expertise with innovation, collaboration, and meaningful problem-solving, we'd love to hear from you! Flexible working arrangements, advanced technology, and collaborative workspaces. A culture of high performance and innovation where we experiment with new ideas and take responsibility for achieving results. A global network of talented colleagues, who inspire, support, and share their expertise to innovate and deliver for our clients. Global Orientation program to kickstart your journey, followed by access to our Learning@MSCI platform, AI Learning Center , LinkedIn Learning Pro and tailored learning opportunities for ongoing skills development. MSCI strengthens global markets by connecting participants across the financial ecosystem with a common language. Title: Senior Data Analyst - Remote - Latin America
Description: About the role We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst to lead the design and delivery of enterprise analytics. Ability to work independently in a remote, fast-paced environment. Kake is a remote-first company with a global community, fully believing that it’s not where your table is, but what you bring to the table that matters. We provide top-tier engineering teams to support some of the world’s most innovative companies, and we’ve built a culture where great people stay, grow, and thrive. We’re proud to be more than just a stop along the way in your career - we’re the destination. The icing on the Kake: 💰 Competitive Pay in USD: Work globally, get paid globally. 🌎 Fully Remote: Simply put, we trust you. 💜 Better Me Fund: We invest in your personal growth and passions. 🎂 Compassion is Badass: Join a community that invests in social good.

Title: Analista de Administración de Riesgos
Description: Descripción de la empresa GO Credit es una empresa financiera líder 100 % mexicana, creada para ofrecer préstamos con descuento vía nómina a trabajadoras y trabajadores de gobierno, educación y salud que no tienen acceso formal al sistema financiero. Desde 2011, el objetivo ha sido facilitar soluciones de financiación y consumo de forma rápida, sencilla y cercana. La empresa cuenta con una estructura sólida, presencia en las principales ciudades del norte de México y más de 100 personas colaboradoras. Su misión es brindar un servicio de alta calidad que fortalezca las finanzas de sus clientes, y su visión es situarse entre las cinco empresas líderes de nicho en México, apoyándose en pilares como mejor precio, producto y servicio. GO Credit se guía por valores como servicio, respeto, honestidad, integridad y competitividad. Descripción del puesto Como Analista de Administración de Riesgos en GO Credit, te encargarás de analizar, evaluar y controlar los riesgos asociados a los productos de crédito personal de la empresa. En el día a día, revisarás carteras de clientes, modelos de scoring y políticas de riesgo, proponiendo ajustes para mejorar la calidad del crédito y reducir la morosidad. Colaborarás con áreas como finanzas, operaciones y tecnología para implementar procesos y herramientas de gestión de riesgos, así como para dar seguimiento a indicadores clave. También participarás en la elaboración de informes, en la documentación de procesos y en la formación interna sobre políticas de riesgo. Este es un puesto de jornada completa, presencial, ubicado en Monterrey, NLE, y puede ofrecerse como contrato temporal según las necesidades de la empresa. Requisitos Aptitudes analíticas sólidas para interpretar datos, elaborar modelos de riesgo y tomar decisiones basadas en indicadores cuantitativos y cualitativos. Aptitudes de comunicación efectiva, tanto escrita como oral, para coordinarte con diferentes equipos y presentar informes claros a personas clave de la empresa. Conocimientos en finanzas, especialmente en créditos personales, gestión de cartera y conceptos básicos de riesgo financiero. Experiencia en gestión de programas y proyectos (program management), incluyendo planificación, seguimiento de hitos y coordinación de iniciativas de mejora de procesos. Capacidad para impartir formación interna y apoyar en la capacitación del personal sobre políticas, procedimientos y herramientas de administración de riesgos. Valorable formación universitaria en Economía, Finanzas, Administración, Matemáticas, Ingeniería o similar, así como manejo avanzado de Excel, herramientas de análisis de datos y conocimientos básicos de normativa financiera. Capacidad para trabajar en equipo, orientación al detalle, alto sentido de responsabilidad y adaptación a entornos cambiantes dentro del sector financiero, conocimienro en SQL ( indispensable).
